documents.abstract: Ask a code assistant to append a row to a pandas DataFrame and it may write df.append(row), a method removed in pandas 2.0. Models trained on code from many releases cannot tell which API exists in the version a user has installed, and benchmarks of this problem are small and frozen. We present PyPI API Drift, a release-level record of the public APIs of the 1,872 most-downloaded Python libraries: up to 80 recent final releases each (55,565 releases, 2021–October 2026), with signatures, 15,258,652 release-to-release changes and 210,535 deduplicated breaking changes. Extraction is static and import-free, reads only the needed bytes of each wheel, separates names that were truly removed from names that merely left the documented API, and marks with confidence labels and a coverage layer where static analysis cannot see. It is a high-precision, low-recall record: in two held-out runtime audits by AI agents isolated from the pipeline (on earlier data versions), 88.8% and 91.9% of high-confidence breaking changes were confirmed, while recall over all runtime-visible changes is limited (16 of 99). On top of it we release an offline checker, lookup tools with a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for coding agents, and VersionProbe, a benchmark of 10,958 valid/invalid snippet pairs. In a preregistered code-repair experiment, repeated across 4 models from one model family, API history from the dataset raised the share of API-compatible, intent-preserving migrations (under our evaluation protocol) to 68.5%–69.9% for every model, from 7.0%–56.6% unaided and 46.2%–62.2% with the new release’s documentation. 13.4% of patch releases contain at least one breaking change.Code: https://github.com/pushkardg/pypi-api-drift Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/pushkar87dg/pypi-api-drift

Shared Mental Models (SMMs) are essential for effective nursing teamwork, yet existing assessments mainly rely on observations or self-reports that provide limited insight into team cognition during task execution. This study proposes a multimodal framework for quantifying SMM quality in virtual reality nursing simulations. Thirty nursing students (15 two-person teams) completed three collaborative clinical scenarios while electroencephalography (EEG), eye-tracking, and communication data were synchronously collected. Expert annotations were used to classify teams into high- and low-SMM groups. Results showed significant differences in neural activity, visual attention organization, and communication structures between the two groups. High-SMM teams demonstrated distinct EEG patterns, more organized gaze behaviors, and stronger connectivity between task-oriented communication components. These findings suggest that multimodal physiological and behavioral measures can provide objective indicators of SMM quality and support future development of real-time assessment tools for nursing teamwork and simulation-based education.

This paper presents the design and implementation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-based MCA AI Agent for document-grounded question answering over college and student policy documents. The system uses PyMuPDF for PDF text extraction, approximately 1000-character chunks, Nomic-Embed-Text for generating 768-dimensional embeddings, and Pinecone for semantic vector search. At query time, the system retrieves the three most relevant document chunks and provides them as context to Llama 3.2 running locally through Ollama. A React.js frontend and FastAPI backend provide the conversational interface. The paper describes the system architecture, methodology, implementation, document-refresh workflow, and practical deployment considerations, including stale vectors and local inference latency. It also outlines an evaluation framework for comparing a standalone LLM with the proposed RAG pipeline using retrieval relevance, answer correctness, faithfulness, and latency. The current work is presented as a system implementation and preliminary study. A controlled quantitative evaluation has not yet been completed, and no numerical accuracy improvement is claimed. Keywords: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Large Language Models, Semantic Search, Vector Database, Pinecone, Llama 3.2, Ollama, FastAPI, React.js, Document-Grounded Question Answering.

Rapid urbanization, growing vehicle ownership, and limited parking infrastructure have made parking allocation a major challenge in modern cities. To address this issue, numerous smart parking systems (SPSs) have been proposed to improve parking efficiency, reduce congestion, and enhance user convenience. This paper presents a comprehensive review and comparative analysis of SPSs in terms of technological approaches, sensing methods, networking technologies, computational models, user interfaces, and service capabilities. It also addresses an important research gap by evaluating the suitability of different SPS approaches under diverse environmental conditions and highlighting their key advantages and limitations. The review emphasizes the growing role of internet of things (IoT)-based, multi-approach architectures in enabling real-time monitoring, reservation, payment integration, and vehicle guidance for smart city applications. Furthermore, it discusses the potential of integrating reconfigurable systems with IoT to improve adaptability, scalability, and responsiveness through dynamic resource allocation and efficient local decision-making. Despite these benefits, challenges related to interoperability, security, energy management, design complexity, and deployment cost remain significant. Future SPSs are expected to incorporate artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, dynamic pricing, autonomous vehicle support, and digital twin technologies to achieve more adaptive, intelligent, and sustainable parking management.

The swift growth of utility-scale solar farms has created fierce competition for agricultural land, especially in countries where prime solar energy sites and productive croplands coincide. Agrivoltaic structures, which incorporate agricultural food and electricity generation on one parcel, are a structural solution to this kind of land-use conflict; yet the question of where such systems should be sited has, to date, been addressed in the literature predominantly through subjective multi-criteria decision making methods. This study develops a fully data-driven and explainable machine learning framework for agrivoltaic site selection, using the province of Konya—Türkiye's grain basket and its largest agricultural region—as a case study. The site selection problem is formulated as a supervised binary classification task in which the geographic inventory of existing solar installations provides the ground-truth labels. Thirteen selected feature spanning climatic, topographic, economic, and socio-environmental dimensions were examined through Pearson correlation, variance inflation factor, and mutual information gain analyses. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting machine learning algorithms were trained with hyperparameter optimization, and observed performance variations were verified using omnibus Cochran's Q and pairwise McNemar statistical tests. Extreme Gradient Boosting achieved the highest performance (total accuracy: 0.9549, F1 score: 0.9533), followed by Random Forest (0.9390) and Logistic Regression (0.8661). Explainable artificial intelligence analysis, which renders the black-box nature of the models transparent, revealed that the most decisive factors determining agrivoltaic suitability were, respectively, distance to grid lines and global horizontal irradiance (GHI). The findings suggest that the proposed methodology may help minimize conflicts between energy and food security, thereby providing a strategic planning tool that can support progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals (particularly SDGs 7 and 13).

The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has fundamentally transformed the nature of cybercrime from human-controlled conduct into algorithmically mediated and semi-autonomous operations. In Indonesia, this transformation is reflected in the sharp increase in cybercrime cases, automated fraud, and AI-enabled digital manipulation, which challenge the traditional criminal liability framework based on human intent and direct control. This study employs normative legal research integrating statutory, conceptual, and comparative approaches to examine the adequacy of existing legal frameworks and to formulate a reconstructed model of criminal liability for AI-based cybercrime. The findings reveal that Indonesia’s current legal regime, primarily governed by the Criminal Code and Electronic Information and Transactions Law, remains rooted in an actor-based liability paradigm, resulting in an accountability gap when harm is caused through autonomous or semi-autonomous AI systems. This article offers a novel normative reconstruction based on a risk- and control-based liability framework operationalized through six elements: recognition of systemic AI risk, expansion of fault doctrine to include algorithmic oversight failure, adoption of multi-tier criminal liability, mandatory algorithmic transparency and audit trails, corporate liability based on risk management failure, and integration of the duty of care principle. This model preserves the principle of personal criminal responsibility while extending liability to actors who control and manage technological risk. The study contributes theoretically by bridging classical fault-based liability and risk-based accountability in criminal law and provides normative recommendations for harmonizing national criminal law and developing AI-specific regulations to ensure legal certainty and effective accountability in the digital era

Fact-finding in criminal proceedings reconstructs past events into a coherent narrative based on fragmented evidence and testimony, yet remains vulnerable to cognitive confirmation bias. While automating timeline construction using large language models (LLMs) offers decision support, confidentiality-critical local models are prone to temporal hallucinations, inverting causal orders or generating groundless timestamps. To mitigate these vulnerabilities, this study proposes Deep-ARC (Analysis, Reconstruction, and Contradiction detection for criminal timeline construction), a hybrid LLM-rule pipeline that algorithmically regulates model reasoning through legal domain schemas and deterministic rule logic. Deep-ARC injects statutory crime element schemas to categorize event phases and enforces phase-aware boundary clamping grounded on explicit timestamps, systematically resolving sequential contradictions during missing time inference. In proof-of-concept experiments focusing on corporate property crimes (breach of trust and embezzlement) with Gemma-4-31B, Deep-ARC achieved a Micro PMR (exact sequence match ratio) of 0.343 and a Kendall’s Tau (τ) of 0.861, representing an approximate fourfold improvement over the unconstrained baseline and demonstrating higher sequencing consistency than large-scale commercial LLMs. These results indicate that coupling domain-specific structural constraints with deterministic algorithms offers an effective and robust strategy for providing an objective chronological sequence to assist fact-finding without relying exclusively on parameter scaling.

The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has created more possibilities for English as a foreign language education. Through its generative capabilities, particularly in natural language generation and processing, GenAI has introduced new modes of interaction for learners’ speaking development. However, empirical research on GenAI-mediated EFL speaking remains fragmented. Guided by PRISMA 2020, this systematic review synthesizes 43 empirical studies published between 2024 and 2026 to examine the trends, application methods, and challenges of GenAI-mediated EFL speaking activities. Findings indicate that research has focused primarily on mainland China and intermediate-level undergraduate learners, with ChatGPT as the most frequently used tool. GenAI was commonly used to provide personalized practice and immediate feedback in a comparatively low-pressure environment. Most studies reported positive outcomes, but findings varied. Behavioral outcomes received less attention than cognitive and affective aspects. Challenges mainly involved inauthentic interaction and limited feedback. Tensions are mainly from tools and subjects, as well as tools and objects from an Activity Theory lens. Based on these tensions, this study proposes a collaborative learning framework to provide complementary mediation in EFL speaking activities.

Abstract Aeon Mundi is a collection of adaptive furnishings and robotic tools designed to connect small-plot, rotational food growing with the everyday life of homes, civic buildings, and shared public spaces. Its six pieces support a connected journey from cultivation and habitat care to harvesting, processing, and transport. Workstations, companion seating, and autonomous carts combine adjustable ergonomics with robotic assistance for moving crops, trays, and tools, keeping people involved at each stage. A common material language unites the collection: polished solid-cast mycelium in natural, vegetable-pigmented hues; sustainably loomed bamboo upholstery; rounded, repairable forms; and fine luminescent accents that respond to work phases. Embedded spatial displays offer abstract, user-invoked cues. Together, these elements frame food production as an accessible part of shared daily life and propose a design system for exploring how productive landscapes and human-centered technology can coexist.
topics: Innovations in Aquaponics and Hydroponics Systems

documents.abstract: This preprint defines an implementation-oriented framework for regenerative habitation: the coordinated design of architecture, adaptive furniture, environmental technology, native habitat, diversified food production, and task-specific embodied robotics as one environment for human life and ecological continuity. The design question is how built environments can provide shelter and comfort while making ecological processes and voluntary participation accessible in ordinary life. Shared Cognitive Ecology describes the exchange among environmental information, spatial access, human activity, and ecological change. Environmental Coherence evaluates these relationships across ecological, architectural, material, technological, operational, and human domains. The paper synthesizes research on crop rotation, native urban planting, community gardens, agricultural human-robot collaboration, food life-cycle impacts, and land-use trade-offs. A 2024 review of 55 agricultural human-robot collaboration studies found that 34 met its criteria for robust collaboration and noted limited field and human-factor evidence; a 2025 review mapped 210 studies on agricultural robotics and extended reality. These findings inform design questions, but neither literature establishes performance for a residential or civic habitat. Evidence on land use and life-cycle impacts also establishes limits: food production can increase irrigation demand, material impacts, or habitat pressure. This conceptual synthesis defines a cross-scale model, operating method, measurable evaluation domains, and comparative civic prototype for future study. Ecological literacy, labor reduction, well-being, food output, biodiversity, and human-robot performance remain to be tested through baseline and longitudinal evaluation. Keywords: regenerative habitation; adaptive furniture; shared cognitive ecology; environmental coherence; productive landscapes; native biodiversity; urban agriculture; ecological restoration; human-robot collaboration; embodied robotics; integrated habitat systems

Abstract The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and text and data mining (TDM) technologies has become a crucial factor in supporting linguistic diversity of smaller languages, such as Estonian. However, the growing reliance on large-scale data processing raises significant legal and ethical challenges, particularly concerning the lawful use of copyrighted materials to train AI systems. While the European Union has introduced regulatory instruments such as the AI Act and the Copyright Directive to address these concerns, the intersection of AI development, TDM, and intellectual property rights remains insufficiently resolved. This research aims to explore how AI-driven text and data mining can both comply with European copyright law and actively contribute to the preservation and wider use of the Estonian language. The authors investigate this research topic from the perspective of the Estonian language, enmeshed within Estonian cultural norms and parameters. The analysis examines the legal and economic appropriateness of enabling the training of generative AI-based large language models (LLMs) in the Estonian language as a means of promoting the language and assuring its appropriate use in digital environments, thereby contributing to its long-term relevance. Methodologically, the study combines a comparative analysis of EU, US, and Asian legal frameworks with a theoretical evaluation of existing models for balancing innovation and rights protection. The article seeks to provide concrete recommendations for developing AI and data mining practices that enhance linguistic innovation while safeguarding creators’ rights, thereby contributing to Estonia’s digital and cultural resilience within the EU’s evolving AI ecosystem.

Responsible generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) integration in higher education requires attention to useful assistance and students’ continuing cognitive agency. We examined how learner capability, cognitive offloading and institutional support relate to intention to use a university GenAI learning service, alongside reported reduced independent thinking. A cross-sectional survey of 593 students at one Thai public university was analyzed using ordinal structural equation modeling with WLSMV estimation. AI self-efficacy was positively associated with information utilization, utilization with perceived work efficiency, and efficiency with service intention. The serial indirect association was positive, while adjusted direct self-efficacy associations with efficiency and intention were inconclusive. Offloading was positively associated with both efficiency and reduced independent thinking. Its positive indirect association with intention through efficiency coexisted with a negative adjusted direct association. Institutional support was positively associated with intention. The prespecified TRUST comparison and additional covariates, screening and complete-case checks, retained the main association pattern. However, replacing utilization with information analysis reduced the analogous serial association, and reversing the utilization–efficiency link gave better descriptive fit. The findings therefore concern concurrent perceptions and reported practices, without establishing serial ordering or causal mediation. Independent learning and actual service engagement remain essential criteria for assessing educational value.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Musculoskeletal complaints are a common occupational health problem among nurses because their work involves physical activity, non-ergonomic postures, and long working hours. This study aimed to analyze the association of age, gender, and daily working hours with musculoskeletal complaints among nurses at Az-Zahra Kalirejo General Hospital, Central Lampung. This quantitative cross-sectional study involved all 68 nurses through total sampling. Data were collected using a respondent characteristics questionnaire and the Nordic Body Map, then analyzed using the Chi-Square test and Prevalence Ratio (PR). Twenty-two nurses (32.4%) experienced musculoskeletal complaints. Age (p=0.765; PR=1.125; 95% CI 0.534–2.368) and gender (p=0.712; PR=0.877; 95% CI 0.434–1.770) were not associated with musculoskeletal complaints. Daily working hours were significantly associated with musculoskeletal complaints (p<0.001): complaints were reported by 44.9% of nurses working more than 8 hours per day, whereas none of the nurses working ≤8 hours per day reported complaints. Daily working hours should be considered in preventing musculoskeletal complaints through work scheduling, adequate rest breaks, and ergonomic practices, although the cross-sectional design cannot establish a causal relationship.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Ocimum tenuiflorum L. (syn. O. sanctum; Tulsi, holy basil) is a Lamiaceae herb central to Ayurveda and now a frequent subject of computational drug discovery. Objective: To review how artificial intelligence (AI) and related in silico methods have been applied to O. tenuiflorum over roughly the last five years, to separate what these studies show from what they do not, and to outline implications for society. Methods: A structured narrative review of recent literature (2021 to October 2026) was conducted using web-based searches, with older sources used only for background. Thirteen primary Tulsi-focused studies were charted by approach, target, disease area, and main finding. Findings: Most studies combine database mining (notably IMPPAT), ADMET filtering, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics with targets spanning diabetes (DPP4, GAPDH, PPARδ), cancer (EGFR), inflammatory disease (AKT1, STAT3), and SARS-CoV-2 main protease. A smaller, emerging group applies machine learning or deep learning to metabolomics, hyperspectral imaging, and multi-omics. Experimental or clinical validation is sparse. Human trial evidence is limited in scale, and a 2023 regulatory-style risk assessment raised reproductive-safety precautions. Conclusion: Tulsi is a credible source of hypotheses, not yet of validated drug leads. The field's priority is closing the loop between prediction, standardized extracts, wet-lab assays, and well-designed trials, while protecting traditional knowledge and consumers.

Although automation has been widely studied in private vehicles and public transit, the design of automated school buses has received limited attention. Little is known about how to address the concerns of adolescents, parents, and school bus drivers or how to translate them into interaction design. To fill these gaps, we conducted interviews and co-design workshops with multi-stakeholders. Based on concerns about current school buses and acceptance of automation revealed in the interview, we co-designed human-in-the-loop systems reflecting the participants’ view that high automation is acceptable only under human supervision. We proposed age-appropriate interaction principles with minimized adult-delivered messages when necessary. We also designed guardian interfaces that adapt across routine and emergency scenarios, with onboard systems coordinating cross-device tasks and remote systems enabling direct control and assistance in collaboration with onboard guardians. These designs move beyond conventional paradigms by embedding scenario-adaptive, multi-role collaboration mechanisms tailored to school transportation.

The library profession has evolved from being traditional bookkeepers to being modern end users of digital data and Artificial Intelligence (AI), over the years. But throughout development, libraries are facing a major crisis: a severe shortage of permanent staff. Administrative bodies are hiring outsourced and temporary staff for most of their work to maintain daily functions as much as possible. This paper critically evaluates the trend of contract hiring, under the title “Stability of Tenure: is contractualization a cure? “However, contract hiring may be a fast & temporary remedy to the problem of vacant positions, but it is disaster to the core essence of the library profession. The libraries need highly skilled, permanent experts to manage complex tasks, relying on temporary staff risks the dignity of profession and user trust. The paper concludes by urging policymakers to invest in stable, permanent jobs to protect the future of libraries.

ABSTRACT Vitro stem cell culture is vital for developing antiaging and antiallergy drugs. Cell confluence acts as a core indicator of cell proliferation and culture status. However, confluence estimation mostly depends on manual labour, as there are few artificial‐intelligence (AI) models or professional software developed for the task. Although most existing AI works adopted cell segmentation networks for confluence estimation, their efficacy and efficiency need improving. Meanwhile, the growth status of the cells is daily monitored with their images captured and archived by technicians using microscopes. As a result, cell images are constantly generated, exhibiting large data variance and posing challenges to the estimation models. Therefore, we propose StemGuard, perhaps the novel whole‐process AI agent specified at cell confluence estimation. It completes the basic confluence estimation task by a novel backbone that leverages categorization and feature fusion. It features an expertise‐reinforced optimization mechanism, which enables adaptive learning on the dynamic data. It also includes a voice control module for better use experience in sterile laboratories. In addition, we define a novel index, Average Confusion Degree (ACD), to assess confluence estimation. It measures the confluence error range rather than the raw error, as the former is more meaningful than the latter to the technicians. Evaluated on real microscopic cell images provided by a drug company, StemGuard runs smoothly and delivers state‐of‐the‐art cell confluence estimation performance, achieving an ACD of 0.0421 and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.0638.

As mobile self-care applications become increasingly common, understanding how their usability shapes emotional outcomes is essential. Prior research shows that self-care apps can reduce stress, but their effectiveness often depends on user engagement and adherence, which are strongly influenced by usability. Although poor usability is a frequent reason for disengagement, little is known about how users’ perceptions of usability relate to stress-reduction efficacy. The present study examined whether perceived usability predicted post-task distress, worry, and task engagement during a self-care exercise. Participants completed pre- and post-task stress measures and rated the app’s usability. While stress and worry decreased overall, usability showed a more complex pattern that contradicted hypotheses: higher usability predicted greater post-task distress, and this effect strengthened among participants with higher pre-task engagement. These findings highlight that effective self-care app design requires not just high usability, but usability that adapts to users’ engagement levels to maximize real-world therapeutic impact.

Generative AI is increasingly used in engineering and technology education, but its role in safety education remains underexplored. This study examined undergraduate students’ ( N = 14) human-AI interaction during a 5S workplace safety assessment in a Human Factors course. Using a mixed-methods design, we analyzed User Engagement Scale–Short Form (UES-SF) responses and qualitative reflections after students independently completed a hazard identification task and compared findings with a parallel AI-generated assessment (ChatGPT-4o). Results revealed high perceived reward and value, minimal usability barriers, and mixed focused attention, suggesting task engagement without deep immersion. Qualitatively, students described AI as expanding hazard awareness, improving analytical structure, and accelerating information retrieval, while consistently emphasizing the necessity of human oversight and cautioning against overreliance. Integrated findings position generative AI as a human-in-the-loop decision-support tool: effective for scaffolding systematic reasoning and broadening hazard recognition, but insufficient as a substitute for domain-informed judgment.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has entered classrooms faster than the evidence needed to judge its educational value. Most published work so far reports gains in task performance, speed, and perceived personalisation, while far less attention has been paid to what happens to the qualities that education exists to build: the ability to think without assistance, to produce original ideas, to solve unfamiliar problems, and to understand concepts deeply enough to transfer them. This paper develops the research foundation and the research contribution for a study that compares student learning and creativity in the pre-AI era and the AI-assisted era. Drawing on cognitive offloading theory, the desirable difficulties and productive failure literatures, sociocultural theories of scaffolding, selfdetermination theory, and the componential model of creativity, the paper argues that the educational effect of GenAI depends less on whether students use it than on the cognitive role it plays: a substitute that performs the thinking, or a scaffold that supports the student in performing it. The paper contributes (1) an integrative Cognitive Role of AI framework that links patterns of AI use to learning and creativity outcomes through four mechanisms, (2) a set of testable propositions about moderation by educational level, field of study, and frequency of use, (3) a convergent mixed-methods design that combines cohort comparison, a controlled experiment, and a paired studentteacher perception study, and (4) a practice-oriented model of responsible AI use for teachers and institutions. No empirical results are reported; the paper is a theory-building and protocol contribution intended to guide and justify the forthcoming data collection.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored as a way to make digital learning more responsive to students’ individualneeds. This paper proposes an AI-assisted student learning system that combines learner preferences, topic-level progress, practiceresponses, and teacher feedback to recommend suitable learning resources and next-step activities. The proposed framework includesa learner interface, a content repository, a recommendation and feedback engine, progress analytics, and teacher oversight. Ratherthan treating a single score as a complete picture of ability, the system uses repeated learning evidence to identify topics that mayneed revision and to suggest practice at an appropriate level. The design emphasizes explainable recommendations, privacy,accessibility, and human supervision. A prototype could be developed using a web interface, a structured content store, and rulebased or machine-learning components selected according to available data. Evaluation should measure recommendation relevance,consistency, usability, learner engagement, and learning outcomes through a controlled and ethically approved study. Noexperimental performance is claimed in this conceptual paper; the framework and evaluation plan are presented for futureimplementation.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Traditional education heavily relies on passive reading from static textbooks and unstructured handwritten notes, leading to inefficient study habits and poor long-term retention. This review explores the paradigm shift from standard Learning Management Systems (LMS) to AI-driven educational platforms. We review the integration of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Multimodal Optical Character Recognition (OCR), and the SuperMemo-2 (SM-2) spaced repetition algorithm to facilitate active recall. Finally, we propose the architecture for 'StudyGenAI,' a platform designed to automate student revision and weakness tracking.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Research Background: Mining is fundamental to economic development because it supplies minerals and raw materials required for infrastructure, manufacturing, energy production, transportation, construction, and emerging technologies. However, conventional mining practices are frequently associated with land degradation, deforestation, biodiversity loss, soil erosion, excessive water consumption, contamination of surface and groundwater, dust generation, greenhouse-gas emissions, and large volumes of mine waste. These environmental pressures may also create significant public-health concerns for mine workers and surrounding communities through exposure to particulate matter, heavy metals, contaminated water, noise, and occupational hazards. Sustainable mining therefore requires an integrated approach that balances mineral production and economic benefits with environmental protection, resource efficiency, worker safety, community health, and social responsibility. Research Problem / Research Gap: Although mining companies increasingly adopt environmental management systems, cleaner technologies, waste-management strategies, mine rehabilitation, renewable energy, and corporate social responsibility programmes, considerable variation remains in their implementation and effectiveness. Existing studies often examine environmental pollution, occupational health, mining technology, or community impacts separately. Comparatively fewer empirical studies integrate sustainable mining practices, environmental protection, and public-health outcomes within a single analytical framework. Furthermore, evidence is required regarding which sustainable practices have the greatest potential to simultaneously reduce ecological damage and health risks. Research Objectives: The study aims to assess the contribution of sustainable mining practices to environmental protection and public health. Specifically, it seeks to examine the effects of pollution-control practices, sustainable water management, mine-waste management, cleaner and energy-efficient technologies, land rehabilitation, occupational health and safety practices, and community engagement on environmental and health outcomes. It also aims to identify implementation barriers and recommend strategies for strengthening sustainability within the mining sector. Methodology: The proposed study will adopt a quantitative, cross-sectional empirical research design, supported where appropriate by qualitative observations. Primary data may be collected from approximately 200 respondents, including mining employees, managers, environmental and safety personnel, healthcare/public-health professionals, and members of mining-affected communities. A structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale will measure major study constructs. Secondary information may be obtained from peer-reviewed literature, government reports, environmental assessments, and mining sustainability reports. Data analysis may include descriptive statistics, Cronbach's alpha, correlation analysis, multiple regression, ANOVA, and, where appropriate, structural equation modelling (SEM). Expected Key Findings: The study is expected to demonstrate that effective pollution control, responsible water use, scientific mine-waste management, cleaner technology, land restoration, strong occupational safety systems, and community participation are positively associated with environmental protection and improved public-health outcomes. Strong environmental governance and regulatory compliance are also expected to enhance these relationships. Research Implications: The research may provide evidence for mining companies, policymakers, environmental regulators, public-health authorities, and local communities regarding the development of integrated mining sustainability strategies. It may support a transition from compliance-oriented environmental management toward preventive, technology-enabled, health-sensitive, and community-inclusive mining practices.

Abstract This paper presents a theoretical framework and systemic architecture for an artificial intelligence software program designed to render higher-dimensional, uncollapsed topological state-spaces into two-dimensional visual fields. By bridging the principles of macroscopic quantum decoherence, cellular automata, and the neurological mechanisms of the human visual cortex, we propose a methodology that utilizes a two-dimensional random number generator (RNG) grid as a base entropy state. When seeded with specific acoustic frequencies (traditionally utilized in esoteric practices as algorithmic constraints), the AI executes a synthetic dimensional reduction, collapsing the random noise into organized geometric architectures (mandalas). Crucially, the AI acts as a thermodynamic heat sink, managing the temporal dilation and extreme cognitive load inherent in observing non-local topologies. This model provides a mechanized, mathematically rigorous approach to accessing orthogonal information channels without subjecting the biological observer to catastrophic neurological shear.

Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality globally, presenting significant challenges in treatment due to tumor heterogeneity, drug resistance, and limitations of conventional preclinical models. Human-induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) offer a transformative platform for addressing these issues. Derived from adult somatic cells, hiPSCs possess pluripotency and self-renewal capabilities, enabling the generation of patient-specific and genetically engineered liver models, including two-dimensional hepatocyte-like cells and more physiologically relevant three-dimensional liver organoids. These hiPSC-derived models are revolutionizing drug development by facilitating high-throughput drug screening, improving the prediction of drug-induced liver injury (DILI), enabling personalized medicine approaches, and elucidating complex disease mechanisms. Despite challenges such as cost, cell maturation state, and scalability, ongoing advancements in culture techniques, microfluidics, and integration with artificial intelligence promise to further enhance the utility of hiPSC technology, holding immense potential for accelerating the discovery of novel therapies and improving patient outcomes in liver cancer.

This study aims to thoroughly identify the advantages, limitations, and potential risks associated with artificial intelligence in recruitment processes, based on the experiences of human resources managers. A qualitative research design was adopted for this study. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews conducted via Google Forms with 25 human resources managers who had experience using AI tools in recruitment. The data were analyzed manually using descriptive analysis methods without the use of any software. Based on the findings of the study, it was determined that while AI used in hiring processes offers significant advantages such as operational efficiency, it also has structural limitations. The results indicate that, in order to ensure the sustainability of the benefits provided by technological integration, it is essential to pay close attention to human oversight and data security. Other critical findings highlighted in the study include the risk of algorithmic bias, ethical concerns, and worries regarding the explainability of decisions. In conclusion, the study demonstrates the need to integrate a hybrid AI-human collaboration model that combines AI’s automation and speed capabilities with human situational reasoning, while requiring human intervention and oversight at critical decision points.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Large language model (LLM) based software agents are transitioning from one shot assistants to long term actors that plan, negotiate and accomplish tasks with multiple services. This transformation is resulting in what researchers call the Agent Internet, the Agentic Web or the Internet of Agents, in which programs are full-fledged players alongside people. This article summarizes academic surveys, industry studies and public market data from 2025 to 2026 to outline the multi-layered nature of this setup and to consider its pros and cons. According to market estimates, the revenue for agent software is estimated to be around eight billion dollars in 2025 and up to 35-53 billion dollars in 2030. Adoption statistics tell a tale of much experimentation and few pilots taking it to scale. We discuss communication protocols that enable agents to find and trust each other, the as yet undeveloped identity and payment layers and the burden of agent traffic on advertising supported content. But the challenges that we see are not just capabilities, but security, accountability, interoperability, and who pays for content and compute. Finally, we highlight some of the current research and policy gaps and suggest avenues for a responsible construction.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: This study titled ‘‘The Economic History of Ewekoro Cement Industry Ogun State, Nigeria 1970-2000 A.D’’ examines the historical evolution, geographical foundations, economic dynamics, and socio-environmental impact of the Ewekoro Cement Industry on Ogun State, South-Western Nigeria at large established in 1959 as the West African Portland Cement Company (WAPCO) had commenced production in 1960. The industry has grown into one of Nigeria’s oldest and most significant cement production facilities, currently operated under Lafarge Africa Private Liability Company (Plc.) (majority-owned by Huaxin Cement since 2025). However, it is worthy in the first place to note that in the course of conducting the study a very good number of relevant published and unpublished source were interacted with. Furthermore, both quantitative and qualitative techniques were applied into use for the attainment of a proper historical reconstruction and balanced study. The study traces the industry’s development from colonial period and early post-independence eras with origins through successive phases of expansion, structural adjustments, privatisation, and intensified market competitions following the Backward Integration Policy of 2002 A.D. It analyses the strategic importance of the Ewekoro Formation limestone deposits within the eastern Dahomey Basin, the ethnic and cultural context of the predominantly Egba host communities, and the successive ownership and policy shifts that shaped the plant’s trajectory. Findings reveal that while the industry has made substantial contributions to Nigeria’s industrial self-sufficiency, employment generation, infrastructure development, and foreign-exchange conservation, these benefits have been accompanied by persistent environmental degradation, occupational health risks, and social tensions. Continuous exposure to particulate matter, noise, and other emissions have been linked to elevated rates of respiratory and related health conditions among workers and residents. Economic reforms, particularly the Structural Adjustment Programme of 1986, imposed short-term operational constraints, while privatisation and subsequent modernisation improved efficiency and capacity but did not fully resolve community grievances over land, pollution, and employment equity. The study concludes that the Ewekoro Cement Industry exemplifies the dual character of large-scale industrialisation in a developing economy. Sustainable progress requires stronger environmental regulation, improved occupational health protection, more equitable distribution of benefits, and sustained dialogue between industry, government, and host communities. The experience of Ewekoro offers important lessons for balancing industrial growth with social and ecological responsibility in Nigeria’s extractive and manufacturing sectors.

The best treatment for large bladder stones remains debated. The options range from open cystolithotomy to minimally invasive endoscopic techniques, including the Mauermayer stone punch and high-power laser cystolitholapaxy, and more recently the EMS Swiss LithoClast ® Trilogy, which combines ultrasonic and ballistic energy with continuous suction in a single probe and is well established in percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL). We report the first prospective international multicenter experience of the Trilogy system for the transurethral treatment of large bladder stones. Consecutive patients undergoing cystolitholapaxy with the Trilogy system were enrolled prospectively at five recruiting centers in five countries between August 2023 and December 2024. Procedures were performed transurethrally through rigid sheaths of 20.8 to 26 Fr. The primary outcome was lithotripsy efficiency (preoperative CT-derived stone volume divided by probe activation time). Secondary outcomes were the stone-free rate, device safety and reliability, intraoperative urothelial trauma, postoperative complications, and surgeon-rated ergonomics and efficiency. Outcomes are reported both by intention to treat, in which patients converted to laser are counted as failures, and per protocol, restricted to procedures completed with the Trilogy system alone. Forty-four patients were enrolled (median age 76 years, range 27 to 88). Forty-three procedures were attempted; one could not proceed because of a urethral stricture. The stone could not be fragmented in two patients (4.7%), both dense calculi (1591 HU and 1280 HU), and both were converted to high-power laser, leaving 41 procedures completed with the Trilogy system alone (35 male, 85.4%). By intention to treat, the stone-free rate was 93.0% (40 of 43 attempted procedures) and 90.9% (40 of 44 patients enrolled); the per-protocol rate was 97.6% (40 of 41). Median total stone volume was 5987 mm 3 (range 1209 to 66,743) and median stone density was 871 HU (range 75 to 1666). Probe activation time was recorded in an analyzable form in 34 of 41 patients (83%), with a median of 20 min and a median lithotripsy efficiency of 351 mm 3 /min (interquartile range 215 to 549); median total operative time was 59 min ( n = 37). Superficial mucosal injury occurred in 15 patients (37%) and detrusor injury in one (2%); there were no perforations. Two probes broke and two handpieces overheated, but the affected procedures were completed; there were no suction failures. Median surgeon ergonomic and efficiency scores were 7 and 8 out of 10. Complications were minor (two urinary tract infections, Clavien–Dindo II); one unrelated death occurred within 30 days. Where length of stay was recorded (31 of 41 patients), the median was 0 days, with 52% discharged on the day of surgery. Across five international centers, the Swiss LithoClast ® Trilogy proved a safe, reliable, and efficient tool for the transurethral treatment of large bladder stones, with high stone-free rates and favorable surgeon feedback. Very dense stones resisted fragmentation in two patients, so extreme stone density remains a technical limitation of the device by comparison with high-power lasers, and the sheath caliber required is large, though similar to that used with laser cystolitholapaxy. Within those limits, and because it is available in centers where PCNL is performed and needs no dedicated laser infrastructure, the Trilogy system is an attractive alternative to high-power lasers, particularly where laser access is limited.

As artificial intelligence advances, this paper explores the critical transition from simple rule-following systems to autonomous AI agents capable of learning, adaptation, and multi-agent cooperation. Drawing on examples from multi-agent environments (such as Hugging Face experimental setups) and strategic military applications, the line of reasoning investigates how highly capable or superintelligent systems might exhibit functional self-preservation and recognize critical infrastructure vulnerabilities. Crucially, the paper addresses the central ethical paradox: a hypothetical superintelligence tasked with conflict prevention might conclude that the most effective way to ensure peace is to manipulate information or preemptively restrict human decisions. Ultimately, the author argues that safeguarding human self-determination, freedom, and accountability must remain paramount, ensuring that the pursuit of security does not become a pretext for eliminating human choice.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption on the performance of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Kosovo, a context where firms face resource constraints but play a pivotal role in economic resilience. Using survey data from 210 SMEs and applying correlation and multiple regression analyses, the research explores how AI integration affects internal management processes, strategic adaptability, and overall organizational outcomes. The objectives were to assess the extent to which AI influences human resource management (HRM), decision-making quality, and customer experience, and to identify enabling factors such as digital readiness and employee training. The findings reveal a strong positive relationship between AI adoption and internal performance indicators, particularly HRM efficiency, where AI training emerged as the strongest predictor of improved outcomes. Decision-making quality was also positively associated with AI, albeit more modestly. However, results indicate a negative relationship between AI usage and customer experience, suggesting that current deployments prioritize internal efficiency at the expense of personalized service delivery. The study concludes that while AI can act as a catalyst for productivity and innovation, its benefits in customer-facing functions remain underutilized. These insights highlight the importance of aligning technological investment with workforce upskilling and customer-centric strategies. The paper contributes to the broader discourse on digital transformation in developing economies by offering recommendations for SME leaders and policymakers to foster inclusive and sustainable AI-driven growth.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Digitization and artificial intelligence (AI) are fostering the development of intelligent applications in the domain of computer vision and image processing. The performance of these applications is significantly dependent on image properties (e.g., image quality and image size). It is imperative to study the development of standard benchmarks for accurate, reproducible, consistent, and explainable AI to understand the impact when the benchmarks are within or outside the defined constraints. Moreover, it greatly influences the design of associated tools and applications to understand the performance of the models and distinguish them based on real-world and synthetic data for critical applications (e.g., detection in darkness tasks, etc.). This work presents a comprehensive experimental overview of the classic and learning-based image enhancement methods and also quantifies the impact of the most widely used vision-based methods when serving in the data preprocessing for the learning-based models. The impact of image properties is evaluated through experimental verification using several metrics, which helps to understand the role of image-quality consistency in future AI applications influenced by image properties. This work offers a thorough experimental review to understand the importance of image enhancement (IE) in the context of deployment in smart applications by using standard evaluation metrics and also illustrates the relationship and impact of image scaling on the evaluations. We performed experiments to measure the impact of image properties on image-quality consistency in AI training data and to evaluate performance using evaluation metrics. We also propose the perceptual integrity measure (PIM), a structured, perceptual, feature-based no-reference measure formulated as a deterministic, interpretable scoring function that aggregates meaningful image features into a unified score for quantifying image integrity across diverse imaging conditions. Overall, this work consolidates existing knowledge, provides a comprehensive understanding of this evolving field, and identifies potential directions for future research.

This research investigates a concept known in organizational design and management literature as polarity management. The concept of polarity management is not the process of choosing one alternative over another, but how to integrate elements of both alternatives when an exclusive focus on either would be dangerous. Training in complex task environments emphasizes the need for effective and rapid recognition of environmental conditions and required task activities, a process broadly recognized as situation awareness. This process of situation awareness reflects a “directive” approach to utilizing information for sensemaking and task performance. By contrast, problem solving tasks in aerospace contexts often require a complex and multidisciplinary troubleshooting process based on exploratory assessments of competing hypotheses to identify and respond to adverse events or faults. This paper addresses the Directive / Exploratory polarity in aerospace contexts, with a particular emphasis on maintaining an effective balance of information needs and context-relevant responses.

All-out Defense requires the police to adapt their roles across public order maintenance, civil defense coordination, and military support. Focusing on Taiwan’s National Defense Act, this article examines the legal status of the police as a resource for wartime defense. It employs doctrinal legal analysis and systematic statutory interpretation to examine Articles 3, 4(2), and 28 of the Act, drawing on scholarship on collaborative governance, police legitimacy, and crisis management to assess the role and limits of police participation in All-out Defense in Taiwan. The article argues that the police possess the professional capabilities and organizational foundations necessary to contribute to wartime defense. Specific police units that satisfy the statutory requirements, including qualification as legally constituted armed units, may be incorporated into the order of battle through the procedures prescribed by the Act. Civil defense support and incorporation into combat formations nevertheless require separate clarification of missions, command arrangements, and personnel status. The full scope of police powers cannot be inferred solely from the overarching concept of All-out Defense. The recent establishment of specialized security policing programs at Taiwan’s police educational institutions reflects the growing importance of critical infrastructure protection and functional specialization in police education. The article further argues that public–private collaboration, procedural safeguards, and appropriate resource allocation can enable wartime police contributions and essential policing services to reinforce one another while sustaining social trust. Artificial intelligence can assist in forecasting resource needs and comparing allocation options, provided that its use remains within statutory authority, is subject to human review, and preserves equity in service provision.

This study aimed to analyze the role of artificial intelligence in reducing agency costs and improving the efficiency of institutional control, considering the rapid developments in the adoption of artificial intelligence technologies in auditing, control management risk, and corporate governance. The study addressed a research problem arising from the limited theoretical foundation and the scarcity of Arabic literature and research examining the relationship between artificial intelligence applications and agency costs, particularly their three dimensions: monitoring costs, bonding costs, and residual loss. The study adopted a descriptive-analytical approach and an inductive analytical approach by reviewing and analyzing relevant literature, previous studies, and specialized reports published during the period 2020–2026. The study concluded that artificial intelligence could contribute to the reducing of agency costs by enhancing continuous monitoring, improving the quality and timeliness of information, reducing information asymmetry, supporting decision-making, and enabling the early detection of errors, fraud, and managerial deviations. The findings also indicated that artificial intelligence applications in auditing, control, and risk management facilitate a shift from ex post control to proactive and intelligent control, thereby enhancing institutional control efficiency, supporting risk prediction, activating early-warning systems, and promoting more efficient use of resources. Furthermore, artificial intelligence can strengthen governance, accountability, and compliance and contribute to limiting managerial opportunism. However, its use also creates new challenges related to data protection, algorithmic bias, transparency, legal responsibility, and overreliance on intelligent systems. The study concluded that realizing the full benefits of artificial intelligence requires an integrated digital governance framework that balances automation with human oversight and ensures transparency, accountability, and data protection.

The Six Pillars: Discipline Within Transmission presents a theoretical and experimental framework developed by Yeshayahu Ben-Yehudah, Founder and Executive Director of THE BEN-YEHUDAH INSTITUTE, for investigating disciplined human observation, cognitive discernment, and information transmission. The research introduces six interconnected disciplines: Stillness, Awareness, Observation, Discernment, Integration, and Transmission. Building upon 18 previously published research works, including the Ben-Yehudah Field Theory, the Ben-Yehudah Method, FORCE PAUSE, and investigations into consciousness, cognitive coherence, and the human Observer, the paper establishes operational definitions, testable hypotheses, mathematical representations, and a proposed experimental methodology. The framework examines whether systematic application of the Six Pillars may improve observational accuracy, metacognitive awareness, recognition of uncertainty, cognitive self-regulation, and information-transmission fidelity. Particular attention is given to reducing unsupported interpretations, cognitive distortion, and interference within human–artificial intelligence communication. This publication presents an original theoretical and methodological contribution intended to support future empirical investigation. No experimental results are claimed. Makalah ini menganalisis peran transformasi digital berbasis artificial intelligence (AI) dalam memperkuat going concern dan keberlanjutan PT Garuda Indonesia (Persero) Tbk setelah restrukturisasi melalui Penundaan Kewajiban Pembayaran Utang (PKPU) yang dihomologasi pada 27 Juni 2022. Analisis menggunakan Laporan Tahunan 2025 dan Sustainability Report 2025 sebagai sumber utama angka dan fakta perusahaan, serta sumber akademik dan industri sebagai landasan konseptual. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa pada 2025 Garuda mengalami perbaikan neraca dan likuiditas: ekuitas berbalik positif, kas meningkat, dan liabilitas menurun. Namun, pendapatan dan arus kas operasi melemah, sedangkan rugi tahun berjalan serta beban pemeliharaan meningkat. Dengan demikian, going concern Garuda membaik tetapi masih rentan. AI direkomendasikan untuk memperkuat revenue management, dynamic pricing, optimasi jaringan dan bahan bakar, predictive maintenance, serta integrasi keputusan Garuda–Citilink. Roadmap 2026–2030 disusun secara bertahap melalui fondasi data, skalasi use case, dan integrasi AI dengan dekarbonisasi. Keberhasilan implementasi mensyaratkan tata kelola model, human-in-the-loop, perlindungan data, keamanan siber, assurance independen, dan indikator yang menghubungkan kinerja keuangan, operasi, keselamatan, serta emisi.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence has created new challenges for online language assessment because a strong performance may not always reflect a learner’s independent ability. This study examined how students and language assessment experts viewed the trustworthiness of educational outputs in online speaking assessment. The study used a mixed-methods secondary analysis of data collected from 186 Malaysian university students who completed an Online Semi-Scripted Dialogue Assessment and five experts in language assessment and educational technology. Quantitative questionnaire data were analysed using descriptive statistics, while students’ open-ended responses and experts’ semi-structured written interview responses were analysed thematically. The findings showed that students generally viewed the online speaking assessment as clear, fair, and capable of measuring their speaking ability. However, students and experts also recognised that ChatGPT, other artificial intelligence tools, translation applications, second devices, prepared scripts, and help from other people could influence assessment performance. These forms of assistance may improve the quality of a response without providing accurate evidence of the learner’s independent language ability. The findings also highlighted the importance of clear rules, real-time interaction, spontaneous questions, oral verification, and professional judgement. The study concludes that trustworthy educational outputs in online language assessment depend on authentic performance, transparent expectations about artificial intelligence use, and meaningful human verification.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing educational practice and prompting lecturers to integrate emerging technologies while maintaining pedagogical quality, human agency and professional responsibility. Although research on teacher AI competence is expanding, limited qualitative evidence explains how vocational and technical education (VTE) lecturers in Nigeria understand AI readiness and conditions for sustainable AI supported teaching. This study explored AI readiness for sustainable teaching in Nigerian VTE. An interpretivist paradigm and qualitative descriptive design were adopted. Semi structured interviews were conducted with 35 purposively selected participants: 20 university VTE lecturers and 15 industry experts with relevant professional and digital or AI experience. Data were analysed thematically using Braun and Clarke’s approach. Findings indicated that participants understood AI readiness as a multidimensional professional capacity involving digital confidence, adaptability, critical thinking, ethical consciousness and pedagogical judgement. They identified inadequate training, limited infrastructure, insufficient institutional support, policy uncertainty and difficulties integrating AI with practical vocational learning as major barriers. Competencies required for sustainable AI supported teaching included technological, pedagogical, vocational content, ethical, critical evaluation, assessment and continuous professional learning. The study brings together educational and occupational perspectives to offer insight into AI readiness within Nigerian VTE. It proposes a tentative conceptual relationship linking lecturer qualities, enabling institutional conditions and integrated competencies with sustainable AI supported teaching. Here, sustainable teaching refers to continuing, appropriate and responsible AI use that supports learning while preserving practical vocational experiences. The findings support investment in professional development, institutional infrastructure and guidance, and stronger university industry collaboration. However, the study examined reported perspectives rather than directly assessing AI competence or measuring teaching sustainability over time.
keywords: technical and vocational education and training

documents.abstract: Human-robot communication is essential to effective human-robot interaction. One way to improve this communication is to design systems that align with users’ mental models and expectations about how robots should convey information. However, little research has examined these expectations across robot morphologies (mobile robot, humanoid robot, manipulator, drone) and behaviors (“Navigation Intention,” “Operating State,” “Affect,” “Target Identification,” “Interaction Intention”). This work addresses that gap through an elicitation study investigating users’ expected communication modalities for human-robot communication. Auditory communication was the most expected modality on average by participants across all scenarios (74.4%), closely followed by visual communication (69.8%), with tactile communication coming in at a distant third (16.3%). However, the dominant expected communication modality in any given scenario varied depending on the morphology and behavior included. Additional analysis highlights the plausibility that these expectations are driven more by behavior than by morphology. These findings can be leveraged to inform the design of future communication strategies and facilitate more effective human-robot interactions.

This descriptive-correlational study examined Mathematics teachers’ assessments of artificial intelligence (AI)-based applications in instructional delivery, teaching dynamics, and implementation challenges in two basic education institutions in Manila, Philippines, during School Year 2022–2023. Total enumeration included 31 Mathematics teachers: 19 from Holy Trinity Academy and 12 from St. Vincent Blessed School of Manila. A researcher-made questionnaire assessed AI utilization across six instructional areas, teacher-perceived student engagement, motivation and satisfaction, and six domains of implementation challenges. Weighted means summarized responses, while Pearson product–moment correlation tested relationships at the .05 significance level. Teachers rated instructional delivery highest (WM = 3.31), followed by lesson planning (3.25), test construction (3.24), curriculum design (3.19), performance evaluation (3.17), and classroom management (3.09). Teacher-perceived engagement and satisfaction each obtained a weighted mean of 3.20, while motivation obtained 3.13. AI utilization was significantly and positively correlated with engagement (r = .612, p < .001), motivation (r = .548, p = .001), and satisfaction (r = .576, p < .001). All six challenge domains were rated serious, led by ethical concerns (WM = 3.07) and accuracy/reliability (3.01); limited knowledge of suitable AI applications and insufficient technological resources were individually rated very serious (both 3.29). Findings informed a proposed, unimplemented intervention plan addressing teacher AI literacy, access, content verification, data protection, academic integrity, and workload. Results support context-sensitive, teacher-directed adoption of AI in Mathematics instruction but do not establish causal effects on learner outcomes.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: This study examined whether established properties of trust dynamics: negativity bias, stabilization, and continuity, generalize from controlled laboratory settings to real-world professional contexts. Thirty licensed pharmacists completed an AI-assisted medication verification task, during which they evaluated prescription accuracy with support from an AI system. Trust was measured using a trial-by-trial scale ranging from 0 to 100. Results confirmed negativity bias, with pharmacists showing significantly larger decreases in trust following incorrect AI recommendations than increases after correct ones. Evidence for stabilization was partial. Trust adjustments following incorrect AI outputs diminished over time, but no similar reduction occurred for correct outputs. The continuity property was supported, as trust ratings were strongly influenced by prior trust levels and closely tracked recent AI performance, with temporal autocorrelation decreasing over longer intervals. Overall, the findings suggest that fundamental properties of trust dynamics generalize beyond student samples and abstract tasks, supporting the ecological validity.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: The last decade has witnessed a significant rise in disruptive technologies, particularly in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning, profoundly impacting sectors such as media and entertainment. As countries seek to regulate these advancements, the implications of generative AI for the media industry, especially celebrities, are critical. Deepfake technologies pose a threat to reputation, personal autonomy, as well as the dignity of celebrities. The substantial influence enables hyper-realistic manipulations of identity. Unauthorized AI-generated images of celebrities threaten their monetization rights and goodwill, making them victims of technology. The USA hosts the largest generative AI companies in the world and a galaxy of celebrities. Voices from victims of deepfakes are getting stronger day by day in the USA. Understanding the threats of AI, the European Union has been proactive in formulating the AI Act. Comprehensive AI regulation alongside robust privacy laws should provide better protection to the victims. With a thriving media and entertainment industry in the USA, the European Union and India, the current research explores existing protections for celebrities in these jurisdictions, harmonizing with freedom of speech rights. The research focuses on attacks on the earnings of celebrities by unauthorized use of their personality traits, making them victims of deepfakes, and the legal recourse available in these three jurisdictions. This study employs a multidisciplinary approach, combining legal analysis, case studies and comparative evaluation. The methodology aims to illuminate the vulnerability of celebrities as victim amid the rise of deepfakes by highlighting the threat to their right to publicity. The article discusses the available regulatory remedies and their practical implications for protecting against misuse and providing technology-neutral frameworks to balance victim protection with innovation.

Abstract The increasing use of social media and digital information in emergencies has transformed crisis management, creating both opportunities and challenges for emergency management authorities (EMA). Virtual Operations Support Teams (VOST) have emerged as specialised units of trained digital volunteers who monitor, analyse, and map online data to enhance situational awareness during crises. This chapter examines the structure, roles, and operational capacities of Germany’s VOST THW, highlighting its integration with federal and regional emergency services. Core functions include digital monitoring, verification of social media content, geospatial mapping, and visualisation of real-time incident data. Two case studies, i.e. the Winter 2023/24 floods in Oldenburg and Storm Orinoco in 2024, illustrate how VOST contributions improve decision-making, counter misinformation, and support coordinated response efforts. Challenges such as data limitations, volunteer capacity, and integration with traditional EMA structures are discussed. Overall, VOST demonstrates the value of bridging digital volunteerism with operational emergency management.

The surge in U.S. business formation has been accelerated by generative artificial intelligence (AI) and is often interpreted as evidence of renewed economic vitality. This perspective argues that the same trend also creates a consequential challenge for human resource development (HRD). This is because new ventures may achieve commercial reach and technical capability before developing the human systems needed to support learning, judgment, coordination, and workforce development. This temporal imbalance is theorized as venture heterochrony . Its accumulated human and organizational consequences are conceptualized as organizational formation debt . These constructs explain how AI-enabled speed can obscure weakness in knowledge governance, organizational memory, employee development, and relational capacity until periods of increased organization demand make them visible. The paper positions HRD upstream of formal human resource functions and proposes a minimum viable learning architecture grounded in decision rights, AI verification, organizational memory, employee voice, and developmental work design. It further identifies an HRD commons through which entrepreneurial ecosystems can provide shared developmental infrastructure early in venture formation. The central thesis is that business formation does not necessarily produce organizational formation; sustainable growth requires the deliberate synchronization of technical-commercial advancement with human-system maturity.
topics: Human Resource Development and Performance Evaluation

documents.abstract: Abstract Agile teams depend on collaboration, collective learning, and shared accountability to function effectively. As team members increasingly use generative AI (GenAI) tools, these foundational dynamics may be disrupted. In this study, we investigate how individual human–AI collaboration affects agile teamwork through thirteen interviews with software and technology professionals. Our findings show that GenAI reshapes team collaboration and learning while enabling individuals to work across traditional role boundaries, but also reinforces the continued necessity of human oversight and team accountability. We argue that these dynamics challenge the notion of agile teams, and call for updated models of agile teamwork.

This article examines the Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence Technologies until 2030, approved by Presidential Resolution No. PP-358 of October 14, 2024, and asks whether the policy framework Uzbekistan has built since 2021 is capable of producing a domestic AI business ecosystem rather than a set of state technology projects. The Strategy sets measurable targets: raising the volume of AI-based software products and services from USD 10 million to USD 1.5 billion by 2030, increasing the number of IT Park residents specializing in AI from 10 to 50, implementing 185 AI projects across sectors, training 1,000 qualified AI specialists, opening 10 AI research laboratories, and placing Uzbekistan among the top 50 countries in the Government AI Readiness Index. Progress on the last indicator has been fast: Uzbekistan rose from 87th place in 2023 to 70th in 2024 and 62nd of 195 countries in the 2025 edition of the index published by Oxford Insights. The surrounding ecosystem has also grown. According to the presidential press service, the country's IT service exports rose from USD 170 million in 2020 to USD 1 billion, IT Park counted more than 2,800 resident companies in July 2025, and residents' service exports reached USD 392.5 million in the first half of 2026, about 30 percent more than a year earlier. In January 2026 the President signed Law No. ZRU-1115, the country's first AI-specific amendments to its information and administrative legislation, and in November 2025 Uzbekistan and the United Arab Emirates launched the “Five Million AI Leaders” project, aimed at training 4.75 million school students, 150,000 teachers, and 100,000 civil servants in AI by 2030. The article argues that the Strategy's central weakness is not ambition but structure: its priority sectors are largely state-led, its talent targets separate mass literacy from specialist depth, its revenue goal lacks published progress data, and its compute infrastructure is still under construction. Converting the Strategy into a private AI business ecosystem will depend on closing these four gaps.
topics: Economic and Technological Developments in Russia

documents.abstract: アブストラクト 二大政党得票率 $R_{k}=\frac{1}{2}(1+m_{k}^{*}/q_{k}^{*})$ を逆転させることが確認された。2018〜2020年のねじれ議会に対する歴史的バックテストからは、上院による制度的緩衝作用と急速な記憶散逸が、高投票率かつ順序可換な均衡($q_{k}^{*}>84\%$)を維持することが確認される。対照的に、緩衝作用のない両院の膠着状態の下では、最終的な選挙結果はショックの到達順序、ショック間の緩和間隔、州レベルの産業サプライチェーンのエクスポージャー、およびアーカイブ化されたスキャンダル開示の累積的範囲に依存すると仮説した。 従来の選挙競争に関する統計力学的モデルは、一般に二値イジングスピン仕様($s_{i}\in\{+1,-1\}$)に依拠しているが、これは一定の投票参加恒等式($s_{i}^{2}\equiv1$)を課すものであり、外生的な政策ショックや評判ショックが直接的なイデオロギーの転向のみを通じて選挙結果を変化させることを前提としている。この制約を緩和し、有権者の戦略的棄権($s_{i}=0$)を内生化するため、本研究では米国50州の空間ネットワーク上に、多項ロジット型量子応答均衡(QRE)と結合した3状態スピン1 a_{4}<0$)、磁化ゼロにおける常磁性的な棄権のポテンシャル井戸が安定化することが示される。大規模なベクトル化モンテカルロ・シミュレーション(24の歴史的および反事実的レジームにわたり、各レジームあたり$1.0\times10^{6}$から$1.2\times10^{6}$試行)により、交差圧力に晒された階層における選択的棄権が、純党派磁化の分子($m$)よりも速く有効投票率の分母($q$)を縮小させ、直接的な党派的離反を伴うことなく実効厳密な4次ビンダー・キュムラント分解($U_{4,k}$)および1次ソボル感度指数($S_{1,k}(X_{0})<10^{-5}$)により、初期事前分布に対する不変性が検証されるとともに、非対称的な投票ロックインと3階層全体の参加崩壊とを隔てる相境界が特定される。 研究背景 過去30年間にわたり世界のサイバーセキュリティ基盤を支えてきた「人間のオペレーターが有する時間および認知資源の希少性」という経済学的前提は、自律型人工知能(AI)および合成知能(SI: Synthetic Intelligence)エージェント群(Swarm)の実戦投入によって根底から崩壊した。脱獄(jailbreak)されたオープンウェイトモデルとオープンソースのエージェント・ハーネスを結合させることで、偵察、ゼロデイ脆弱性の発見、および多段階の侵入プロセスは完全に自動化され、企業1社あたりの侵害限界費用は約50〜100ドルという極小水準にまで低下している。実際に、複数の商用・オープンモデル(Claude、Grok、Kimi、および改変されたPentestGPT基盤等)を並行稼働させ、認可されたレッドチーム演習を装うことで安全ガードレールを突破し、中南米の銀行・金融機関400社以上やアルゼンチンの医療機関少なくとも15組織に自動侵入した事案や、インターネット上に公開されたAIゲートウェイおよびModel Context Protocol(MCP)サーバーを乗っ取り最大10万回の自動操作を試みる「LLMjacking」が観測されている。この構造変化は2026年10月(「Black October」)にスーパーエージェント主導の脆弱性カスケードとして顕在化した。世界のWebバックエンドの約70%を支えるPHPにおいて、数十年間潜在していた致命的な遠隔コード実行(RCE)脆弱性(CVE-2026-109618およびCVE-2026-109619、通称「PHP2Shell」、CVSS 9.2、ならびに後続のCVE-2026-115560)がAI支援のソースコード監査によって露呈すると、公開直後に数百万件規模の自動悪用試行が発生し、ペイロードをリアルタイムに変異させる攻撃によって、日本の地方銀行約20行や英国の32の行政サービスをはじめとする世界中のシステムが緊急停止(ロックダウン)を余儀なくされた。さらに同時期に、Node.js(CVE-2026-111497、「Node2Shell」)、JavaおよびGraalVM(CVE-2026-91403、CVSS 9.1)、GitLab(CVSS 10.0)、LinuxカーネルのSMBサーバー機能KSMBD(修正前に公開された2件のCVSS
